_doc: Copy to ~/.config/yesopen-gpu/config.json (or $YESOPEN_GPU_HOME/config.json). For Verda set up the Verda CLI and fill verda.instance_type and verda.ssh_key_id (gpu.py verda-check checks both); for any other server set provider to other and host (or GPU_HOST), and leave verda alone.
_provider: verda (default): machines are made and deleted with the Verda CLI, which must be set up first; gpu.py verda-check says what is missing. other: any server you or a teammate made (set host, or gpu.py use ADDRESS)
_host: the server's address when you made it yourself (any provider, or a machine in your office); gpu.py up fills it for Verda
_ssh_key: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_yesopen_gpu -C yesopen-gpu; add the .pub key at your provider
_skill_dir: the skit skill the editor runs; empty = the folder that holds this gpu/ folder

verda._instance_type: 1B200.30V: 1x B200 180 GB, $6.987 an hour on demand; fallback 1H200.141S.44V ($4.779); list: verda instance-types --gpu
verda._ssh_key_id: verda ssh-key add --name yesopen-gpu --public-key "$(cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_yesopen_gpu.pub)", then verda ssh-key list. A team sharing one Verda project lists every member's key id here (["id-1", "id-2"]), so whoever starts the machine lets the others connect to it too
verda._location: a location with a free card: verda availability --type <type>. The kept disk stays in the location of the first up, so later sessions start there too.
verda._os_volume_size: GiB of NVMe, $0.20 per GiB a month while kept; Verda disks only grow, enlarge to 400 before variant B
